mathematical_claims.anchor: An odd prime different from five is a square plus five times a square if and only if it is one or nine modulo twenty.
An odd prime different from five is twice a square plus twice the product plus three times a square if and only if it is three or seven modulo twenty.
The prime ideals over three are nonprincipal.
